card.name: Inside rhetorical or exasperated questions
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of rhetorical, scolding or incredulous questions and remarks, such as 'How long are you going to' or 'Boy, I didn't teach you well'. It fires on the small words that come before the sting of the question.

modes.label: Challenge question
modes.description: Words inside a rhetorical 'How long are you going to...' challenge.
modes.example: where Elijah boldly declared, “How long are<< you>> going to be paralyzed by indecision?

modes.label: Exasperated remark
modes.description: Words in a scolding or sarcastic aside, where an emphatic ending is likely.
modes.example: Boy, I didn’t teach<< you>> well enough in 13 years it

modes.label: Skeptical question
modes.description: Words in a doubtful question about whether something is true or likely.
modes.example: Are there really<< that>> many university students in the country who have

card.writes: It favors Chinese exclamation words like '真是' and '难怪' and punctuation such as '?!', which suggests an emphatic or exclamatory ending.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of scolding or doubtful questions, just before the emphatic part.
